profile.reading:
Per Equinix own site, this CH1 facility is located at 350 E Cermak Rd, 5th Floor, Chicago, IL 60616 and totals 107,295 sq ft. Redundancy: N+1 Power redundancy, N+1 Cooling redundancy. No MW power capacity figure is published on this page. 350 E Cermak is one of the most connectivity-dense carrier-hotel buildings in the US, hosting multiple competing data center operators on different floors; Equinix's CH1 suite occupies the 5th floor of this shared, multi-tenant facility rather than a standalone building.

Equinix, the operator, was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson and has grown into a global colocation and interconnection provider operating more than 260 data centers across over 70 metros worldwide; the company converted to a real estate investment trust (REIT) in 2015. Chicago is positioned by Equinix as the fourth-largest primary data center market in the US and a hub for its financial-services ecosystem, connecting trading firms, exchanges, and technology vendors via Equinix Fabric interconnection, cross-connects, and Equinix Cloud Exchange, alongside cloud on-ramps for AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and IBM Cloud.

CH1 sits in Chicago's South Loop at 350 E Cermak Road, one of the most carrier-dense buildings in North America and the historic anchor of the city's data center and telecom-hotel corridor; Equinix's own Chicago financial-ecosystem materials position the metro's combined campus as core infrastructure for the city's futures and options exchanges and the trading firms that colocate near them, alongside cloud on-ramps and thousands of cross-connects concentrated in the Cermak Road buildings.

Equinix's Chicago financial-ecosystem materials describe the metro campus overall as serving derivatives and equities trading firms that colocate for latency reasons near matching engines, alongside enterprise and cloud customers; CH1's specific position within the shared 350 E Cermak building means its connectivity value comes partly from the dozens of other network and content operators occupying different floors of the same structure, a rare shared-building arrangement compared to Equinix's typical practice of operating standalone IBX buildings.

reading.body:
Equinix's CH1 facility in Chicago is a 107,295 square foot building in the city proper with N+1 redundancy for both power and cooling, but the operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for this specific building. Without power capacity data, the scale of AI hosting here cannot be assessed from published sources.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities with only 6 publishing power capacity totaling 236 MW. This facility's rank of seventh by published megawatts in the state indicates either that unpublished capacity exists here, or that five other Illinois facilities each exceed this building's undisclosed power envelope. Equinix operates six buildings across the Chicago metro region, but the operator does not break out individual power allocations by suburb or building online.

For readers tracking AI infrastructure, this facility remains unquantified. The absence of a published power figure, combined with the building's central Chicago location and integration into a regional metro campus, suggests operational capacity that serves enterprise and financial services demand, but cannot be weighed against other data centers or factored into grid constraint analysis without operator disclosure.
